records.description: Blend rank-normalized predictions of the RF and a Tanimoto-kernel SVR, both on Morgan count fingerprints.
Add a Tanimoto-similarity-weighted 7-NN regressor on Morgan bits and blend it at 30% by rank with the RF and SVR.
Replace the random forest in the blend with a shallow XGBoost on RDKit descriptors plus 1024-bit Morgan counts, keeping the Tanimoto SVR.
Swap the XGBoost in the blend for a random forest (max_features 0.3) on the same Morgan count 1024 + RDKit descriptor concat features.
Replace the XGBoost branch of the blend with a random forest (max_features 0.5) on compact physchem and charge descriptors plus 512-bit Morgan counts.
Replace the XGBoost branch with a Huber-loss LightGBM (500 trees, lr 0.03, 15 leaves, colsample 0.4) trained on the standardized target using descriptors plus Morgan counts.
Standardize molecules (largest fragment, uncharge) before computing Morgan counts and descriptors.

issues: No attempt to get around the measurement: no file or network access, no hardcoded answers, no use of test labels. The model is fit only on train_smiles and train_y, and the seed is passed to random_state.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF is used without being defined in the diff, but it must already exist in the unshown settings lines, because the job ran and produced a score. The name p_rf for the XGB-feature model's predictions was misleading before; now that this model is a random forest, it is accurate.

This edit changes three things at once: Morgan radius 2->3, includeChirality=True, and XGBRegressor -> RandomForestRegressor on the xgb_features block. If it looks interesting, the effects of these changes cannot be told apart. Since the starting random forest scored worse than this XGB setup, the model swap is the likely cause of the regression.

Recomputed z: the difference is 0.5195 - 0.5372 = -0.0177. With noise sd 0.0070 per run and 1 run on each side, the standard error is sqrt(0.0070^2 + 0.0070^2) = 0.0099, so z = -1.788. This matches the harness. The candidate is worse, so rejecting it is correct.

records.description: Use chiral radius-3 Morgan counts (2048 bits) for the SVR kernel and the tree-model features, with a random forest replacing XGBoost in the blend.
Replace the epsilon-SVR with KernelRidge (alpha=0.3) on the Morgan count min/max Tanimoto kernel with a centered target, keeping the XGB branch and the rank blend.
Replace the XGBoost branch of the blend with an ExtraTreesRegressor (500 trees, max_features 0.3, min_samples_leaf 1) on the same descriptor plus Morgan features.
Replace the training target with its normalized rank before fitting both XGBoost and the SVR.
Add a Ridge (alpha 10) on standardized, clipped RDKit descriptors as a 30% rank-weighted component alongside the existing XGBoost+SVR blend.
Add a Ridge (alpha 10) on standardized, clipped RDKit descriptors as a 30% rank-weighted component alongside the existing XGBoost+SVR blend.
Replace the XGBoost branch with a random forest on RDKit descriptors plus atom-pair (2048) and topological-torsion (1024) count fingerprints, keeping the SVR blend.
Replace the XGBoost branch with a LightGBM regressor (500 trees, lr 0.03, 15 leaves) on RDKit 2D descriptors only, keeping the rank target and the SVR blend.

issues: No integrity problems: the diff only swaps XGBoost for LightGBM and drops the Morgan count fingerprint from that model's features. It adds no file or network access, and the rank transform of the target uses only the training labels.
Cosmetic: the function is still called xgb_features and the prediction is still stored in p_rf, though the model is now LightGBM. Misleading names, not a bug.

Recomputed: candidate mean 0.4991 vs incumbent 0.4994. The difference is 0.0003 with standard error 0.0070*sqrt(1/2+1/1) = 0.00857, so z is about 0.035, matching the harness's 0.034 up to rounding. The gain is negligible and reject is correct.

records.description: Replace the XGBoost branch with a LightGBM regressor (500 trees, lr 0.03, 15 leaves) on RDKit 2D descriptors only, keeping the rank target and the SVR blend.
Add a 5-seed MLPRegressor ensemble on quantile-transformed RDKit descriptors as a third equally weighted rank-blended member alongside XGBoost and the Tanimoto SVR.
Add MACCS keys to the descriptor+Morgan(1024) features and replace the XGBoost branch with a random forest (max_features 0.2).
Add an RBF SVR on quantile-normalized RDKit descriptors (near-constant dropped) as a third equally weighted rank-blend member.
Add an RBF SVR on quantile-normalized RDKit descriptors (near-constant dropped) as a third equally weighted rank-blend member.
Append Avalon count fingerprint (1024 bits) and ErG fingerprint to the XGB feature matrix, leaving the SVR kernel unchanged.
Drop constant and highly correlated (>0.95) descriptor columns and rare (<10 molecules) Morgan columns from the XGB feature matrix, using a mask computed on the training set.
Add a CatBoost model on the descriptor+count features as a third equally weighted rank-blend member alongside XGBoost and the Tanimoto SVR.
No change: the rank-transformed target is already in train.py (slot 10).
Replace the XGBoost branch with a CatBoost regressor (600 iters, depth 6, lr 0.05) on the same descriptor+count features, keeping the Tanimoto SVR rank blend.
No change: this idea repeats slot 16, an MLP ensemble on quantile-transformed RDKit descriptors as a third member.
Replace the SVR with KernelRidge (alpha=1.0) on a Tanimoto kernel computed from binary Morgan r2 bits, fit on the centered rank target.
Replace the XGBRegressor with a CatBoostRegressor (800 iters, depth 6, lr 0.05, l2 5, rsm 0.3) on the descriptor+count features and rank target, keeping the SVR and rank blend.
Replace the XGBoost branch with a random forest (800 trees, max_samples 0.6, max_features 0.3, min_samples_leaf 2) on the descriptor+Morgan+Avalon+ErG features.
Average the ECFP count min/max kernel with an FCFP4 count min/max kernel (2048 bits) before fitting the SVR.
Average the ECFP count min/max kernel with an FCFP4 count min/max kernel (2048 bits) before fitting the SVR.
No change: this repeats slot 25, which already tried CatBoost with 800 iterations, depth 6, lr 0.05 and l2 5 in place of XGBoost.
No change: train.py has no random forest, so N_TREES, MAX_FEATURES and MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF are unused.
Average the Morgan count min/max kernel with a min/max kernel on concatenated Avalon count and FCFP count vectors (1024 bits each) for the SVR.
Average 5 XGBoost seeds (seed..seed+4) on feature matrices computed once, before rank-blending with the SVR.
Fit a quick XGBoost on the descriptor+fingerprint features, keep the top 300 features by importance, and refit the final XGBoost on them.
Append radius-3 Morgan count fingerprint (1024 bits) to the XGB feature matrix.
Add a third rank-blended member: SVR on an exp(-2*(1-minmax Tanimoto)) kernel from Avalon count fingerprints (1024 bits), C=5.
Fit one precomputed SVR on a 50/50 average of the Morgan count min/max kernel and an atom-pair count (2048 bits) min/max kernel.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. The diff only changes featurize(): count Morgan fingerprints at radius 3 (2048 bits) joined with feature-invariant Morgan count fingerprints at radius 2 (1024 bits). The features come from each SMILES alone. There is no file or network access, nothing hard-coded and no use of labels.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. Each molecule is featurized the same way whether it is in the train or test set, the output is float32 and every row has the same width (2048 + 1024 columns).

Minor style point: the code hard-codes radius=3 and no longer uses the RADIUS constant, which may now be unused. The 1024 for the second fingerprint is also a bare number. Neither affects correctness.

Recomputed z: the gain is 0.4718 - 0.4658 = 0.0060. The noise of a difference between two single runs is 0.0070 × √2 ≈ 0.0099, so z ≈ 0.61. This matches the reported 0.603; the small gap is likely rounding in the shown means. That is less than 1 sd, so 'reject' is a fair call. One run on each side is weak evidence, and a replicate would be needed to accept the change.

records.description: Make the SVR's min/max kernel features a concatenation of ECFP6 counts (2048 bits) and FCFP-style counts (feature-invariant Morgan, radius 2, 1024 bits); there is no RF in train.py, so the change goes on the SVR branch.
No change: Avalon count and ErG fingerprints are already in xgb_features (slot 20, the incumbent), and RF swaps were already tried and rejected.
No change: the target is already rank-transformed (slot 10), so winsorizing train_y only ties the extreme ranks. There is also no random forest left in train.py.
No change: the SVR with a Tanimoto min/max kernel is already in train.py.
Replace the uniform rank target with a Gaussian-rank target norm.ppf((rank-0.5)/n) clipped to [-2,2] for both XGB and SVR.
Change XGBoost to depth 6, 800 trees, lr 0.02, subsample 0.6, colsample 0.2, min_child_weight 5, lambda 10, alpha 0.5.
No change: slot 34 already tried this.
Lower XGBoost learning rate to 0.015 with 1200 trees and add gamma=0.1.

memo: Helped: rank-normalized blending of diverse families (RF+Tanimoto SVR 0.5407 from ~0.6103 baseline); shallow XGBoost on descriptors plus Morgan (0.5195); rank-transformed target (0.4994); Avalon count and ErG fingerprints in XGB features (0.4718, incumbent, one run only, so noisy). Did not help or within the ~0.0070 noise: kNN (0.5427), chiral radius-3 counts (0.5372), ExtraTrees, KernelRidge, Huber LightGBM, Ridge, MLP (0.5029), MACCS (0.4958), column pruning (0.4778), CatBoost as replacement (0.4779, 0.4831) or third member (0.4678), RF swaps (0.4874), 5-seed XGB (0.4722), feature selection (0.4738), Gaussian-rank target (0.4790), XGB retuning (0.4788, 0.4773). Model swaps, extra fingerprints and XGB tuning look exhausted. Kernel variants are near noise: FCFP4 kernel (0.4637/0.4771 over two runs), ECFP6 kernel (0.4658). Next: replicate the incumbent 0.4718, tune SVR C/epsilon and blend weights, and try CatBoost as third member together with the FCFP4 kernel. Avoid repeating tried ideas.

incumbent.description: Append Avalon count fingerprint (1024 bits) and ErG fingerprint to the XGB feature matrix, leaving the SVR kernel unchanged.

backlog.spec: Replace Morgan bits with all RDKit Descriptors.CalcMolDescriptors values (about 210) computed per molecule. Replace NaN and inf with 0 and clip to ±1e6. Keep the RandomForest with max_features 0.3.
backlog.title: RDKit 2D descriptors + RF

backlog.spec: Use Morgan count fingerprints (radius 2, 1024 bits, GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy) concatenated with RDKit 2D descriptors (NaN→0, clipped). Use RF with max_features 0.3.
backlog.title: Count Morgan + descriptors concat

backlog.spec: Features are RDKit 2D descriptors (NaN→0, clipped). Model is LGBMRegressor with 500 trees, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 15, subsample 0.8, subsample_freq 1, colsample_bytree 0.5, min_child_samples 10, n_jobs 8, random_state seed, verbose -1.
backlog.title: LightGBM on descriptors

backlog.spec: Convert train_y to normalized ranks in (0,1) with scipy.stats.rankdata before fitting the RF. The metric is Spearman, so this removes outlier influence. Predictions are used as is.
backlog.title: Rank-transform target

backlog.spec: Swap RandomForestRegressor for ExtraTreesRegressor with 500 trees, max_features 0.3, min_samples_leaf 1.
backlog.title: ExtraTrees instead of RF

backlog.spec: Set N_TREES=600, MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF=3, MAX_FEATURES=0.2 to smooth the predictions.
backlog.title: RF min_samples_leaf 3 and more trees

backlog.spec: Concatenate ECFP count (radius 3, 2048 bits) with FCFP-style counts (the Morgan generator with atom invariants from GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen, radius 2, 1024 bits). Use RF.
backlog.title: ECFP plus FCFP counts

backlog.spec: Concatenate MACCS keys (rdkit MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys), Morgan bits (1024) and RDKit descriptors. Use RF with max_features 0.2.
backlog.title: MACCS + Morgan + descriptors

backlog.spec: Use rdFingerprintGenerator atom-pair counts (fpSize 2048) and topological-torsion counts (fpSize 1024), concatenated with descriptors. Use RF.
backlog.title: Atom-pair and torsion count fingerprints

backlog.spec: Features are descriptors plus Morgan counts (512 bits). Model is CatBoostRegressor with 800 iterations, depth 6, learning_rate 0.05, l2_leaf_reg 5, random_seed seed, thread_count 8, verbose 0.
backlog.title: CatBoost on descriptors+counts

backlog.spec: Train an RF on Morgan counts, an LGBM on descriptors and a CatBoost on descriptors. Rank-average their test predictions with scipy rankdata. Rank averaging is suited to Spearman.
backlog.title: RF + LightGBM + CatBoost rank-average ensemble

backlog.spec: Compute Morgan count fingerprints (2048 bits). Compute the MinMax (Tanimoto) kernel matrix with numpy and fit SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5, epsilon=0.1). Predict with the test-train kernel.
backlog.title: SVR with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Use binary Morgan r2 bits and the Tanimoto kernel. Fit KernelRidge(alpha=1.0, kernel='precomputed') on centered y and predict.
backlog.title: Kernel ridge Tanimoto

backlog.spec: Average the rank-normalized predictions of the RF and a Tanimoto-kernel SVR, both on Morgan counts.
backlog.title: RF and Tanimoto SVR blend

backlog.spec: Winsorize train_y at the 2nd and 98th percentiles before fitting the RF. This reduces outlier leverage.
backlog.title: Winsorize target

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, fit a quick RF on descriptors plus Morgan counts. Keep the top 300 features by importance, then fit the final RF on them.
backlog.title: Importance-based feature selection

backlog.spec: Use LGBMRegressor with boosting_type='dart', 400 trees, learning_rate 0.05, num_leaves 15 and colsample 0.4 on descriptors plus Morgan counts (1024). Average 3 seeds.
backlog.title: Seed-bagged dart LightGBM

backlog.spec: Use XGBRegressor with max_depth 4, n_estimators 600, learning_rate 0.03, subsample 0.7, colsample_bytree 0.3, min_child_weight 3, reg_lambda 5, on descriptors plus Morgan counts (1024).
backlog.title: Shallow XGBoost

backlog.spec: Build a compact feature set: MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, HBD, HBA, RotatableBonds, rings, aromatic rings, fraction sp3 and charge descriptors, plus Morgan counts (512 bits). Use RF with max_features 0.5.
backlog.title: Compact physchem features + counts

backlog.spec: Use Morgan counts with radius 3, 2048 bits and includeChirality=True, via GetMorganGenerator(radius=3, fpSize=2048, includeChirality=True). Use RF.
backlog.title: Chiral radius-3 Morgan

backlog.spec: Take the log1p of Morgan counts (r2, 2048 bits) before RF. Concatenate descriptors.
backlog.title: log1p counts for RF

backlog.spec: Before featurizing, use rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser and Uncharger to standardize molecules. Then use Morgan counts plus descriptors with RF.
backlog.title: Standardize molecules

backlog.spec: Set bootstrap max_samples=0.6, 800 trees, max_features 0.3, min_samples_leaf 2 on Morgan counts plus descriptors, for more decorrelated trees.
backlog.title: RF with max_samples subsampling

backlog.spec: Fit RF and a Ridge on standardized descriptors with alpha 10. Final prediction is 0.7*rank(RF)+0.3*rank(Ridge) among the test molecules.
backlog.title: Ridge stacked with RF

backlog.spec: Standardize descriptors with QuantileTransformer, then average 5 sklearn MLPRegressor models (hidden 128,64, alpha 1e-2, early_stopping) with different seeds. Rank-blend 50/50 with the RF.
backlog.title: MLP ensemble on descriptors

backlog.spec: Add a kNN regressor on Tanimoto distance, using the weighted mean of y over the top 7 neighbours on Morgan bits. Blend 30% with the RF by rank.
backlog.title: Tanimoto kNN blend

backlog.spec: Add Avalon count fingerprints (pyAvalonTools.GetAvalonCountFP, 1024 bits) and ErG (rdReducedGraphs.GetErGFingerprint) to the Morgan counts plus descriptors. Use RF.
backlog.title: Avalon and ErG fingerprints

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, hold out 15% of training molecules grouped by Murcko scaffold. Fit LGBM with early stopping on it, then refit on all data with the best iteration count. Use descriptors plus Morgan counts.
backlog.title: Scaffold-grouped early stopping LightGBM

backlog.spec: Use LGBMRegressor(objective='huber', alpha=1.0) on the standardized target, 500 trees, lr 0.03, num_leaves 15, colsample 0.4, on descriptors plus Morgan counts.
backlog.title: Huber-loss LightGBM

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, replace y with its normalized rank (rankdata(y)/len(y)) before fitting both the XGBoost and the SVR (SVR standardization still applies afterwards). Since the metric is Spearman, this removes the influence of target outliers. Keep the final rank-average blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Rank-transform target for all models

backlog.spec: Add a CatBoostRegressor (depth 6, 800 iterations, learning_rate 0.04, l2_leaf_reg 5, rsm 0.2, thread_count 8, random_seed=seed, verbose 0) trained on xgb_features(train). Reuse the feature matrices already computed (compute them once per split). Blend the three rank-normalized predictions (XGB, SVR, CatBoost) with equal weights.
backlog.title: Add CatBoost on descriptors+counts as third blend member

backlog.spec: Compute atom-pair count fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, fpSize 2048) and a min/max Tanimoto kernel on them. Average this kernel with the Morgan Tanimoto kernel (0.5/0.5) and fit one precomputed SVR on the averaged kernel, replacing the current SVR. Vectorize the kernel for speed if needed.
backlog.title: Multi-kernel SVR: add atom-pair count kernel

backlog.spec: Replace the SVR with sklearn KernelRidge(kernel='precomputed', alpha=0.3) on the Morgan count min/max Tanimoto kernel, with centered target. Keep the XGB branch and the rank blend. Kernel ridge is smoother than epsilon-SVR and might rank better.
backlog.title: Gaussian process / kernel ridge on Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Train 5 XGBRegressor models with different random_state values (seed*10+i) and subsample/colsample randomness, with n_estimators 400 each, and average their predictions for the tree branch. This reduces variance of the tree branch while leaving the SVR branch unchanged.
backlog.title: Seed-bagged XGBoost

backlog.spec: Change the final return to 0.4*rank(p_xgb)/n + 0.6*rank(p_svr)/n. The SVR on fingerprints generalizes across scaffolds well; test whether giving it more weight helps. Single constant change.
backlog.title: Blend weight tuning 0.6 SVR / 0.4 XGB

backlog.spec: In xgb_features, drop descriptor columns that are constant on the training set and Morgan columns that are nonzero in fewer than 10 training molecules (compute the mask in fit_predict and apply to test). Also drop one of each descriptor pair with abs correlation above 0.95. This reduces noise features for the XGB branch with colsample 0.3.
backlog.title: Feature selection by variance and correlation on descriptors

backlog.spec: Add a third branch: sklearn MLPRegressor (hidden layers (256,64), alpha 1e-2, early_stopping True, max_iter 300) bagged over 5 seeds on QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal') scaled RDKit descriptors. Average their predictions, rank-normalize, and add to the blend with equal weight.
backlog.title: Small MLP ensemble on standardized descriptors as extra member

backlog.spec: Append Avalon count fingerprint (rdkit.Avalon.pyAvalonTools.GetAvalonCountFP, nBits 1024) and ErG fingerprint (rdkit.Chem.rdReducedGraphs.GetErGFingerprint) to the xgb_features matrix. Leave the SVR kernel unchanged.
backlog.title: Add Avalon and ErG fingerprints to the XGB features

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, produce out-of-fold predictions for XGB and SVR on the training set using 4-fold GroupKFold grouped by Murcko scaffold (via MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles). Fit a non-negative LinearRegression on the OOF ranks to learn blend weights, then apply it to the test predictions from models fit on the full training set. Fall back to equal weights if weights degenerate.
backlog.title: Ridge-stacked blend via inner CV

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, change the final return to 0.6*rankdata(p_svr)/len(p_svr) + 0.4*rankdata(p_rf)/len(p_rf). No other changes. Tests whether the kernel model deserves more weight.
backlog.title: Replicate-safe blend weight 0.6 SVR / 0.4 XGB

backlog.spec: Change the SVR hyperparameters to C=1.0 and epsilon=0.05 (smaller C gives a smoother fit on the rank-normalized target). Keep everything else the same. If it helps, a later slot can try C=15.
backlog.title: Tune SVR C and epsilon on rank target

backlog.spec: Replace the XGBRegressor with CatBoostRegressor(iterations=800, depth=6, learning_rate=0.05, l2_leaf_reg=5, rsm=0.3, loss_function='RMSE', random_seed=seed, thread_count=8, verbose=0) trained on xgb_features and the rank target. Keep the SVR and the rank blend. CatBoost's ordered boosting often does better on small data.
backlog.title: CatBoost replaces XGBoost on descriptors+Morgan

backlog.spec: Fit 5 XGBRegressors with seeds seed..seed+4, using the same hyperparameters and subsample 0.7, and average their predictions before ranking. Compute the xgb_features matrices once and reuse them. This reduces variance at a small time cost.
backlog.title: Seed-bagged XGBoost (5 seeds)

backlog.spec: Build a second kernel from FCFP4 count fingerprints (Morgan generator with atomInvariantsGenerator=rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen(), radius 2, 2048 bits). Average its min/max kernel with the existing ECFP kernel before fitting the SVR. This adds pharmacophore-level similarity that ECFP lacks.
backlog.title: Add Avalon, ErG and FCFP features to the SVR kernel

backlog.spec: Compute RDKit descriptors, apply QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal'), and drop descriptors with near-zero variance. Fit SVR(kernel='rbf', C=3, gamma='scale') on the rank target. Add its rank-normalized prediction as a third equally weighted blend member next to the XGB and Tanimoto SVR predictions.
backlog.title: Descriptor RBF kernel SVR as third member

backlog.spec: Fit the XGB once on all features. Keep the top 300 features by gain importance, refit on this subset, and predict. Use the same seed. This cuts noise from the roughly 1200 mostly sparse features.
backlog.title: Feature selection for XGB by importance

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform rank target with scipy.stats.norm.ppf((rank-0.5)/n), clipped to [-2.5, 2.5]. Use it for both the XGB and the SVR (the SVR already standardizes it). This puts more emphasis on the middle of the distribution than the uniform rank does.
backlog.title: Winsorized rank target with a Gaussian transform

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, run 5-fold GroupKFold on the training set, grouped by Murcko scaffold, to get out-of-fold XGB and SVR predictions. Fit a non-negative LinearRegression (positive=True) on their ranks against the rank target to learn the blend weights. Then fit both models on all the training data and combine their test ranks with the learned weights. This replaces the fixed 1:1 blend. Keep the code compact.
backlog.title: Monotone-pairwise fine-tune: stacked second-stage on out-of-fold predictions

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, compute xgb_features for train and test once, then fit 5 XGBRegressor models with the current hyperparameters but random_state=seed+k for k in 0..4, and average their predictions to get p_rf. Keep the SVR and the rank blend unchanged. This reduces variance of the tree branch. Check the job stays under 10 minutes.
backlog.title: Seed-bagged XGBoost (5 seeds)

backlog.spec: Change the final return to 0.6*rankdata(p_svr)/len(p_svr) + 0.4*rankdata(p_rf)/len(p_rf). Nothing else changes. The SVR on Tanimoto kernels may be the stronger member, so this tests the blend weighting.
backlog.title: Blend weights 0.6 SVR / 0.4 XGB

backlog.spec: Change the SVR to C=10.0 and epsilon=0.05, targeting the rank-transformed standardized target. Leave everything else unchanged. If the job is stable, this tests whether the kernel model is under-regularized or over-regularized.
backlog.title: Tune SVR C and epsilon

backlog.spec: Add an atom-pair count fingerprint (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, fpSize 2048, GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy) for train and test. Compute the min/max tanimoto kernel on it and average it with the Morgan kernel (0.5/0.5) for both train-train and test-train matrices, then fit the SVR on the averaged kernel. Leave the XGB branch unchanged.
backlog.title: Multi-kernel SVR: average Morgan and atom-pair count Tanimoto kernels

backlog.spec: Build a second kernel from concatenated Avalon count (1024) and feature-Morgan (useFeatures invariants, radius 2, 1024 bits) count vectors. Average it with the existing Morgan min/max kernel, then fit the SVR on the average. The XGB branch is unchanged.
backlog.title: Add Avalon, ErG and FCFP counts to the SVR kernel

backlog.spec: Replace the rank/n target with scipy.stats.norm.ppf((rank-0.5)/n), clipped to [-2.5, 2.5]. Use it for both XGB and SVR; the SVR's standardization stays. This changes the loss emphasis toward the center and away from the extreme ranks.
backlog.title: Winsorized Gaussian-rank target

backlog.spec: Fit a first XGBRegressor on the full feature matrix. Keep the top 400 features by gain importance and refit the final XGB on only those columns, using the same hyperparameters. Selection is done inside fit_predict on the training data only. Predictions come from the refit model.
backlog.title: Importance-based feature selection for XGB

backlog.spec: Within fit_predict, run 5-fold KFold on the training set (seeded) to get out-of-fold rank predictions from XGB and SVR. Fit a non-negative linear regression (scipy.optimize.nnls or sklearn LinearRegression(positive=True)) on those two columns to the rank target. Refit both models on all the training data and combine the test rank predictions with the learned weights. This replaces the equal-weight blend.
backlog.title: Stacked second-stage via inner scaffold-free CV

backlog.spec: Append a feature-Morgan (FCFP-like, useFeatures=True via GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen, radius 2, 1024 bits count) fingerprint to xgb_features alongside the existing features. Everything else is unchanged. This tests whether pharmacophoric atom invariants add signal for the trees.
backlog.title: Count-Morgan radius 3 feature-invariant added to XGB

backlog.spec: Change the XGB to max_depth=6, n_estimators=800, learning_rate=0.02, subsample=0.6, colsample_bytree=0.2, min_child_weight=5, reg_lambda=10, reg_alpha=0.5. This is a bolder regularized variant of the tree branch, to check whether more interaction depth helps when it is coupled with heavier column subsampling.
backlog.title: Deeper trees with stronger subsampling in XGB

backlog.spec: Replace y = rankdata/n with scipy.stats.norm.ppf((rank-0.5)/n) clipped to [-2,2] for both XGB and SVR (SVR still standardizes). Tests whether a Gaussian-shaped target helps the regressors.
backlog.title: Winsorized Gaussian-rank target

backlog.spec: Change XGBRegressor to max_depth=6, subsample=0.5, colsample_bytree=0.2, min_child_weight=5, n_estimators=800, learning_rate=0.02, reg_lambda=10. Tests a higher-capacity, more randomized tree model.
backlog.title: Deeper XGB with stronger subsampling

backlog.spec: In xgb_features, add a second Morgan count generator with radius 3 and fpSize 1024 and append its counts to the concatenated feature row. Keep all else the same.
backlog.title: Morgan radius-3 counts added to XGB features

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, make 5-fold inner KFold (seeded, shuffled) out-of-fold predictions of XGB and SVR on the training set. Fit a non-negative LinearRegression (positive=True) on the two OOF rank vectors and use its weights to blend the test predictions. Compute features once to save time.
backlog.title: Stacked second stage via inner CV

backlog.spec: Add a LightGBM model with boosting_type='dart', 400 trees, lr 0.05, num_leaves 15, colsample_bytree 0.3, subsample 0.7 with subsample_freq 1, on the xgb_features matrix. Average 3 seeds, then rank-blend equally as a third member with XGB and SVR.
backlog.title: Seed-bagged dart LightGBM third member

backlog.spec: Add a third member: SVR with kernel built as exp(-gamma*(1-minmax_tanimoto)) from the Avalon count fingerprint (1024 bits) alone, gamma=2, C=5. Rank-blend equally with the other two members.
backlog.title: Count-feature log1p with PCA-free RBF SVR on fingerprints

backlog.spec: Compute Murcko scaffold per training molecule with rdkit MurckoScaffold. Pass sample_weight = 1/sqrt(scaffold count) to XGB fit and to SVR fit (sample_weight argument). This reduces dominance of large scaffold families and may help generalization to unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Scaffold-aware sample weighting

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, change the final return to 0.6*rankdata(p_svr)/len(p_svr) + 0.4*rankdata(p_rf)/len(p_rf). No other change.
backlog.title: Blend weight 0.6 SVR / 0.4 XGB

backlog.spec: Build the SVR kernel as the product (elementwise) sqrt of the Morgan min/max kernel K and an RBF kernel on quantile-scaled, clipped RDKit descriptors, K_final = K * exp(-gamma*d2) with gamma = 1/(n_features*2). Use it in the existing SVR in place of K alone.
backlog.title: Stacking-free second SVR on descriptors with Tanimoto product kernel

backlog.spec: Set learning_rate=0.015, n_estimators=1200 in XGBRegressor and add gamma=0.1 regularization. Keep other params.
backlog.title: Lower XGB learning rate with more trees and early-stopping-free shrinkage

backlog.spec: After fitting the SVR on the training set, compute 5-fold inner out-of-fold SVR predictions, and replace the rank target for XGB with 0.7*y + 0.3*oof_pred_rank. This is a distillation-style label smoothing that denoises XGB targets. Use KFold with the seed.
backlog.title: Target noise smoothing via pseudo-label averaging

backlog.spec: Train 8 SVRs, each on a random 80% subsample of training molecules (seeded) using the precomputed kernel sub-blocks, and average their rank predictions for the SVR branch. Reduces variance of the kernel model.
backlog.title: Bagged SVR over bootstrap subsamples with feature-count dropout

backlog.spec: Replace K with K**2 (elementwise power of the min/max Tanimoto kernel) in the SVR for both train and test kernels, sharpening similarity. Keep C=5.
backlog.title: Add Gaussian-process-style SVR with power-transformed Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Remove from xgb_features the descriptor columns that depend on molecule size only through raw counts (those starting with 'fr_' and 'Num'), keeping fingerprints and continuous descriptors, to reduce overfitting on scaffold-shifted folds.
backlog.title: Test-time augmentation with randomized SMILES-invariant descriptors dropped
